tips.comment: Dare To Shout has switched to chasing this season. Although only winning one of his six chases so far, he has finished second in the other five. He tries as far as three miles two furlongs for only the second time, having run here last March at this distance over hurdles, again finishing second but finishing off the race well. He has every chance off his current mark of 132; his win came off 128.

Still sits 7 lbs above his last winning mark. To be fair, the way he won on that occasion would suggest he's still got plenty to give off a mark like this. He drops back in trip this time, having pulled up in the Edinburgh National last time out. Clearly didn't stay the trip. He bolted up on his second chase run at Wetherby, absolutely battering Farnoge, with a 15L gap separating them at the finish. He's yet to show that form in his two runs since. For me, he had his excuses: non-stayer last time out, and outclassed in a Grade 2 novice the run before that. He gets his beloved quicker ground today. All his best form has come on quicker ground. He won both of his points runs, so clearly made for chasing. If he can get back to his old form, I think he can win again off this mark.

Lucinda Russell may have this sown up with her two runners. YOUR OWN STORY won't go off at 9/2 in my view, and he looks the pick of the pair at the early prices. A consistent chaser who probably has no stamina limitations, this trip is going to be short enough, but the small field and change of headgear may just see the 9-year-old enjoy himself. He has a nice low weight, and although he handles softer, it doesn't seem to matter too much what the ground is like. Hopefully, his rider will take the trouble to weigh in and secure prize money, wherever the pairing finishes.
Was only 10/1 to win the Grand National last year. Looks well handicapped off 150, as has gone well off higher marks in the past and C&D to suit.
Won in listed grade two starts back in a very small field. I'd say this is slightly tougher. Drops back in grade today and can still improve, so is the one to beat.

In terms of the two currently heading the market, I Am Max goes up five pounds in the ratings whilst Ballyfort goes up nine pounds. Following wind surgery, he carried twelve stone to win by eleven lengths over a two-mile trip. Today he goes up in class and, as a consequence, has ten stone eleven pounds on his back. Providing the extra half mile suits and he continues to benefit from recent wind surgery, with the same jockey on board, Ballyfort could go in again.
Has been running well this season and looks like an improving type. Has won a maiden hurdle and was 2nd on handicap debut. More to come here at a big price.

FOSTER'S FORTUNE has been steadily progressive for the past year and there is every reason to think he can go close in this. As a punter, it is really important not to bet in 'qualifiers' and that structure is a really flawed concept, in my view. However, this is the final so everyone is out to do their best. This 6-y-o is stepping up in trip today on ground he will love and his overall profile just looks right. He may even have qualified three times!

Third of sixteen over course and distance off this mark of 109 and under today's jockey Brian Hughes in April 2024 on soft ground, weakening on the run in. He won his next race at Perth over a furlong shorter off a pound higher mark in May 2024 and not seen again until November 2024. He has disappointed in all 4 starts since that win at Perth but has been racing off higher marks, will strip fitter for those runs and of interest back below that winning mark.

The Jewellers Pet is a 6 year-old gelding trained by Ian Duncan. Progressive type that has shown some real form over hurdles recently with his last 3 handicapped outings providing a 3rd, 1st and 1st, (at Class 5, 5, and 4 company) with the most recent run being 26 days ago, albeit these were on soft, soft and heavy ground. The going at Kelso at time of writing is good but showers likely overnight. Running at a favourable weight with a claiming jockey on board, this looks like a nice each way bet.

Looks the correct price, so not much face value. However, the favorite (who looks the most likely winner) trainer is out of form, and that may mean it won't run to form. This could easily pick up the pieces ahead of the rest, and a safety net of 5 places, in my opinion, makes it a good bet.

Interesting price here for a horse who won last time out at Doncaster by two lengths when wearing cheekpieces. This is because Ashington has only worn them twice so far and won the previous time also when form was also hit and miss at that point. Up 4 lbs here, but could be an each-way opportunity.
Won two of his last four starts. Obviously needs to improve again to take it, but Ellison is a good trainer who could get the required amount out of him. CD is to suit.

A fairly wide open heat, and a chance taken on Ridin Solo who has been beaten off this mark but gets an added claim of 5 lbs from Charlie Maggs. He’s gone well fairly consistently, and I think there’s enough in his form to suggest he can make an impact off an adjusted mark of 100 and from bottom weight in here. He’s unlikely to get a solo up front, but a light weight and front-running tactics could have some of these at it from a fair way out with the right fractions. 4/5 a place on undulating tracks, and 4/5 a place with an uphill finish adds to the intrigue for me, and he won’t mind any extra rain.

Whilst I appreciate the fact that this horse is 9lb higher in the handicap now than when winning over C&D on her last visit to the course, there's no getting away from how well she seemed suited by it and how well she won. The same jockey is back on board now, and he's been excelling for this trainer. He's not been on board for the horse's 2 runs since, but he's back on here, and the horse has been freshened up with a little break. Could go well off bottom weight and looks overpriced to me.

The trainer's runners are on fire at the moment, and Feargal has been using the wind op well on many of his winners. It's a tool that he's been using to good effect for sure. This mare was actually having her second wind op before her run last time out, which was an easy win in a maiden hurdle where the third has since won off a 5lb higher mark than Northern Air races off here. The fourth and fifth have also won since too. This all looks like good enough form to take this off this lenient-looking mark.

Surrey Belle is a nicely bred mare by Golden Horn. She was a three-time winner on the flat and having changed yards, she made her move into the hurdling sphere just before the turn of the year. This five-year-old made an encouraging start over the smaller obstacles, finishing second on her first two starts before securing back-to-back wins, firstly over 2m on heavy ground and then winning by 57 lengths over 2m4f on good ground last time out. Both of those were in novice company and despite having to carry top weight now entering a handicap for the first time, a mark of 121 may well underestimate her ability. She appears to be a versatile sort who has looked like a fluent hurdler. She should be able to make her presence felt in deeper waters today.

Looks well treated from a lowly mark of 105, considering it qualified for this race first up this season with an easy novice hurdle win in a 3-horse race at Plumpton on decent ground. Not disgraced in 2 further runs on softer ground in a higher level of novice race. 6L behind a 116-rated horse LTO.

Has 1 win and 2 placed efforts from 4 runs over hurdles this season. Win came on good at Uttoxeter over 16f with placed runs at Wincanton over 15.5f on good to soft and 23 days ago at Ludlow over 16f on soft, showing ground versatility. Has had a second wind operation since last run and makes the very long journey from D. Pipe's yard with the in-form J. Tudor booked for the ride.
Tom Bellamy's charge comes here in good nick and must be respected after beating Rula Bula by 17 lengths. That was after a wind operation, and there's no reason why she can't repeat that.

Progressive mare who completed the hat trick in Newbury handicap in December added to her tally when winning an 11-runner Taunton mares novice last month. Ran okay at Cheltenham in 9th, a stiff task at the weights, but each way NAP.

The trainer had a 40/1 runner-up in the finals at Musselburgh yesterday, and I am taking a punt on her having this unheralded 6-year-old cherry ripe for the day. She had a decent winner in Velasco in the finals last year, so has shown she can target one.

Fergal O'Brien's second string, LELOOPA, could pick up some decent prize money herself. After showing some promise in Ireland for a smaller profile yard, she quickly found her feet for her new stable; winning her maiden and then a novice hurdle last backend. The tongue tie has helped and she should also enjoy the prevalent ground conditions. Owned by the Paddy Brennan Racing Syndicate, I can see her leaving a disappointing handicap debut last month behind her.

Had good French form, winning when most recently seen over there over hurdles, and won on UK debut. Bit surprised at the odds, as he must have a perfectly reasonable chance of winning again here if improving.

Flash Du Pistolet won off a low mark of 93 last time after showing promise. It was a first time over 2m 4f, so it's odd to see them revert to 2 miles. Perhaps the improvement was more about the jumping than distance, so getting weight off the rest here might enable a quick follow-up.

BOLLINGERANDKRUG landed a hat-trick over C&D back in 2023. He has not won in seven starts since but his last winning mark was 121 and so the handicapper is giving him every chance off a mark of 109 today. At ten years of age, he is not a progressive type but he does have the form in the book to be winning a race of this nature. The concern is that he may not be allowed to lead this field. This gelding has been seen to best effect when allowed to dictate matters up front. If able to get to the front, this runner will hold very strong claims.

Beat a few home in bumpers. Nothing special as of yet, but there's always room for massive improvement with such an unexposed profile. From Dan Skelton's yard, so big things can be expected. CD to suit, hopefully.

I saw Kiwi Rush winning at Kelso last time, and was impressed with him. He was by far the pick of the paddock that day, and won with a bit in hand. This is tougher, however there is every reason to believe he will have stepped forward again from that run.
Won a PTP in April. 5th on debut under rules in a decent bumper. Can only improve, and this race can't be much better. Has an obvious chance of improving.

Has a lot of talent as has been shown by running in Grade 2 contests. I would expect him to bounce back now down to this Class Two company. Lewis Saunders takes the ride claiming 7lb, which is sure to help.

Gentleman Bill has looked a progressive hurdler this season, and was raced in the very competitive Morebattle Hurdle last time. He got a bit run off his legs there, so the step back up in trip here should be to his liking. This isn't as strong a handicap either, and I think we should see him involved.
Second in this race two years ago, and it doesn't look much better. So, every chance of going one better after that promising second effort last time out.
Looks a great each way bet. In my opinion, it looks to have the best chance under these conditions. A bit out of form, but against this field, I've priced it around 10/3. Looks a top bet.

Kept on well when winning over this trip at Wetherby last month and is a previous course winner over 2 miles here. Up 4 pounds as a consequence of that recent success, but that is negated by the 7-pound allowance claimed in the saddle by Harry Atkins and of interest effectively 3 pounds below that winning mark.

Back on his last winning mark, that success coming last March. Is the sole runner on the card for Sheena West who has only sent two runners to the track in her career of over 1000 runners, picking up a 16/1 winner with one of them.

Too Cool Forshrule, a former pointer, had shown very little in four runs over hurdles to get his lowly mark of 86. But six days ago, in a handicap chase at Market Rasen over two miles one furlong on good, he took it up two out, was clear at the last, and won comfortably. Switching back to hurdles without a penalty, he could also show improved form to win again in this two mile three furlong handicap hurdle.

Regal And Royal has improved in his 5 hurdle races. The drier ground and this course and distance have been especially beneficial as he's been here twice and won. A four-pound penalty might not prevent a hat trick.

Worth an each-way saver. Won well 4 runs back and then was unlucky not to follow up, having unseated at the last when looking the likely winner. Disappointed on heavy ground last time. This better ground will probably suit.
Won at 40/1 two starts back in a massive field. Looks like good form, and that wasn't his true running last time out. Worth giving him another chance. CD to suit.

Rhodias' best runs have come on good ground, which he gets today. Both times were over 2m in a bumper 2nd and 2m at Doncaster last January. All other races have been on slower ground. He has shown this trip suits him well, and after returning sound following a fall on the penultimate start, more will surely be asked of him today.
Disappointed last time after having won 3 runs back and then conceding first run in follow-up attempt. Has got an each-way chance in this.
Second at the CD in May at much shorter odds, so getting some value today. Could easily recapture that form and could go one better for Jonjo.

Looks to have the best chance. However, the race is very hard to predict. Should be around 4/1, so take the each way price while you can. Doesn't have any concerns and looks the best handicapped in the race. Express Sunshine will challenge strongly, however.
Won two chases before blotting his copybook in his last race at Hereford. But heavy going that day may well have been behind that run and he should go close here in this company today.

11-year-old but a useful strike rate, although yet to win for a while. But has been in form, placed on all 4 starts since return. Ran well on only trip over course and distance, but career best needed to win.
Won over this course and distance last year off 2lb higher weight, has been out of form but now looks on a handy weight and likes the course.

The gelding had a successful debut over fences at Ludlow in October and has shown commendable performances despite some losses since then. While the challenging conditions at Hereford may not have suited him last time, there are other contenders that seem more promising. However, at the current odds of 12/1, the 7-year-old presents good value for each-way bets.

One Last Glance was well ridden by today's rider to win over 2m5f at Fakenham on the penultimate start. Back on board today with a 5lb claim, and he looks like one who will enjoy the step up in trip on better ground. The price appears generous at 12/1.
Used to be rated much higher, and it wasn't long ago he was winning races off high 80s and 90s marks. Clearly very talented and could still take this being out of the weights.
Won well at Sandown on handicap hurdle last time. Despite a five-pound rise, he should, in this company, be able to continue his good form with distance and the going fine today.

The stable does well here, and this horse steps up in class but was an easy 5L winner last time out at Doncaster. The second has franked the form by winning a decent handicap at Musselburgh on Friday, so the 7lb rise should be workable at the right end of weights here.
Has been very well backed. Had some good form at the start of the season, but since has been disappointing. Could bounce back in these conditions.
Was fourth last time out, which was a slight improvement on previous outings. Is starting to become well handicapped and is certainly more consistent than most.

The standout bet on the card for me. Has run very well in defeat, and none more so than in a decent listed contest when leading for most of the race but getting headed over the last, finishing a close 3rd. Gets 7lb from her main danger here, and the 2m 4f trip should enable her to see this out in front. Lots to like.

Slightly overpriced. I think the favorite may lose the race as it won't be suited to the trip. I reckon this is the only horse in the race with enough to pick up the pieces. Looks decent value at 2/1 as it should be around 13/8.

2nd on debut in a bumper, and it was a good race, so has shown ability even though it might not look like it, beaten some distance in 3 runs since. Still learning though and just needs to jump better.

Taking a punt on the Yeats handicap debutant. No idea how good he is as he's just been pootling about to get an opening mark, but 6-year-olds have a very decent record in handicap hurdles this calendar year, so worth a cheeky each way.

Norn Iron has not had many races for a seven-year-old, just five in total: a bumper and four hurdle races. He is still a maiden but has never finished worse than 4th, with two 2nd places this season. His best performance was here at Newbury when a close 2nd to Bucephalus in January over two miles. He goes up in distance here to two miles three furlongs in his second handicap at the same mark of 114 after being nearest at the finish when 4 lengths 4th at Doncaster last time.

Serious Challenge was a very good flat horse, running at pattern level and being rated 102 on his last start. He's shown a good aptitude for hurdles, winning his last two after an educational first start, and beat a good Elliot yardstick by 9L last time out. That came on heavy ground but with his flat pedigree he should relish a return to quicker conditions and a rating of 128 looks to leave loads of scope after just three hurdle starts and his exploits on the level. Yard in really strong form and all set for a big race.

His level of form stepped up last time when comfortably winning by 7 lengths at Doncaster and looked in control a long way out. Progression is assured with trainer Nicky Henderson and has only had 3 runs.

Skipped cleared by 25 lengths in November 2024 and then followed that up by cantering 8 lengths clear. Both were in a class 4 at Taunton. Had a 3-month layoff and returned to action in a listed novice hurdle. Should go well now back in class 3 company. Looks like he's on the drift, and a bigger price may be available on the day.
Jackpot des Bordes looks very well handicapped on the best of his form. The horse he beat 2 runs ago is now rated 130, which if taken at face value makes the selection look really well treated.
Won three of his last five and needs to improve again, but he's capable. Many of the runners are out of sorts, and this one could improve past them.

Saint Segal is getting smashed in. 6/1 this Friday evening and now coming into 7/2 at 21:00. Opened the season poorly but has progressed nicely, going on to win at Newbury off a mark of 129 by 11 lengths in a class 3, before going back in the weights and going close again for 2nd place by 2 lengths at Musselburgh. He has since returned to Newbury in the Greatwood (Grade 3) going a respectable 5 length 3rd.

John Jo has his horses bang on for this last part of the season. I think Bob Bob Ricard will run a big race. Loves the ground, course, and to me, that matters. Jockey is okay, so big things today in a race that won't take much winning.

Yet to win in 6 races over fences but placed in 3 of those races and all over further. Sent off as favourite for the Plate Handicap Chase at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival over this trip but fell early. Disappointed in 3 races since and not seen since December 2024, but could go well fresh with recent wind surgery offering the potential for improvement.
Came back to form last time out at Huntingdon, has been well backed and looks on a handy mark only 1lb higher than last winning mark.

Another horse who comes in here with plenty to prove at present, but also boasts decent form in the book. The only reservation I would have is the quicker ground. He's only run on it once. To be fair, he ran well on that occasion, beaten 6L by the winner Hunters Yarn, back in 2nd place. He did have Inothewayurthinkin behind him, however. Although he's yet to show any worthwhile form for this stable, he's had his excuses. He likely needed the run on reappearance. He ran okay in the Peter Marsh. I just think the trip stretched him. He struggled off 12st last time out, beaten a distance back in 3rd place. Maybe the weight on soft ground did him in. He's now down to a mark of 139, with the first-time cheekpieces and tongue tie going on. His form for his former stable suggests he's got plenty to give off this type of mark. He did win a Grade 2 novice and also beat the recent Gold Cup winner Inothewayurthinkin in a beginners chase the run before that Grade 2 win.

Comes into this with a bit to prove at present, but very much is a ground-dependent horse. He gets his correct conditions this time, which will help him massively. He's only had 3 chase runs to date. On chase debut, he proved himself to be a chaser to keep on the right side of. He won a 4-runner handicap off this mark at Ascot, beating Bad just over 1L. He showed great battling qualities to repel the challenge of Bad. He also made a crucial mistake at the 2nd last fence. To recover from that and go on to win says a lot about him. He also gave 7 lbs in weight to the winner. That form looks better now with the runner-up winning twice since, with the latest victory coming off a mark of 134. He's pulled up in his 3 runs since. Personally, I don't think he handles soft ground at all, so happy to overlook those runs in the hope the better ground can spark an improved effort. He's got a nice racing weight, which helps. If he can get back to that Ascot form, he looks to have room for maneuver off this type of mark.
Won two of his last three and worth forgiving the pulled-up effort last time out. A trainer like this could easily get him back to his best. CD to suit.
Very progressive and will surely love this extra distance. A competitive first handicap but Jonathan Burke can guide her to victory.

This looks a hot listed Novice hurdle with Slog Geal being the main contender. Jasmine Bliss however, has put out some top efforts this year most recently winning by 11 lengths in a class 4 novice hurdle.

This horse has shown a decent level of form and is very consistent. She won well at Warwick earlier in the season, and although the stable's second string, she looks to be well-weighted and should handle the underfoot conditions.

Up in distance, second last time, and should do better. Trainer has three in this race, and the stable jockey has chosen this one. Has to be given serious consideration. Great each way chance with extra places on offer at 11/1. NAP Each Way.

This Irish-trained mare looks to hold a strong each-way chance here. Her form from her Chepstow victory in October reads well. She goes well fresh, her trainer is in good form, and she gets the services of a top claimer.
Has been running well in hurdles this season and now making a handicap debut. Probably has more improvement to come in these ideal conditions.
Come on Nia, disappointed last time out at Ffos Las on heavy ground. She will be much happier on this quicker surface and is closely handicapped with Crazierthandaisy on her running at Warwick.
Looks a class above these and will enjoy getting back on some decent going. Didn't enjoy the soft going at Wincanton.

JOHN BARBOUR remains an unexposed six year old having had only four career starts and one start over hurdles. He won a 2m bumper at Uttoxeter on his first start for this yard at the beginning of this season. He was fourth on his next start before finishing second to the 138-rated No Questions Asked in a novice hurdle last time out. He stayed on well that day and pulled well clear of the third. He hurdled well throughout and back on similar ground today, he holds strong claims with improvement expected.

The trainer does well with this profile of horse. Won sole start in France on the flat last September, now owned by the Jago family. Gets considerable weight off the odds-on favorite, carrying just ten stone four pounds. Might reward us at a decent price.
2nd in an Irish PTP. Henderson horse now and he will get the full improvement out of the horse. Nico booked. Very unexposed and could take this
Tough to get away from this one at big odds, given he has won a PTP and went perfectly well under rules last time out for a trainer and jockey who won it last year.

This is always a very good bumper and was won last year by the highly promising Regents Stroll. There are some very promising looking horses, but I really like the look of My Fortune who has a great pedigree. He is by Milan, out of a Bob Back mare who has produced plenty of good horses. He has been entered numerous times over recent weeks so should be ready to do himself justice in this hot contest.

Teddy Blue followed his Huntingdon win with a three and a half length triumph at Kempton last week and is quickly turned out off a four lb higher rating. Harry Derham's seven-year-old makes only his fourth chase start and could have plenty more to offer so he can complete the hat-trick.

No stranger to winning over hurdles, Major Fortune has made a promising start going chasing. He pushed higher-rated rival Mahons Glory all the way at Leicester last time. The drop back in distance looks like a strange move here, but there are reasons to be doubtful about some of the opposition's chances, and he's chosen to progress.
Got some headgear on today, which could improve him. Was 4th last time out, and that's not good enough. Needs to improve, but it's possible for a good trainer.
Possible two-horse race as the other market leader has won its last two. This one, for me, has more improvement in the tank left and a good trainer-jockey combo.

Another horse who prefers a sounder surface, which he gets today. He's just 2 lbs above his last winning mark, which should help. Although admittedly, he's never won off a mark this high, his overall form would suggest this mark certainly isn't beyond him. He tends to run well at this track. He also boasts a CD win, which helps, of course, having won this race off a 10 lbs lower mark last term. His form this season would suggest he can defy that 10 lbs higher mark. He won a competitive handicap at Chepstow on reappearance, finding plenty to fend off Pull Again Green. He then finished a decent 3rd behind Chianti Classico at Ascot off a 2 lbs higher mark than this, beaten just 4L. His most recent run was okay, finishing a beaten 2nd behind Tightenourbelts. That horse was well in off that mark, plus this fella carried 12 st, so no disgrace there. If he runs his race, he should be thereabouts.

Daaris looks the way to go here was last seen at Lingfield 17 days ago where finishing 5th/9 and did shape better than that bare result suggests with the drop in trip not suiting too on that occasion however he has an extra 1 furlong 219 yards at his disposal here and that will play greatly into his strengths has met a couple of these rivals before in past races and he meets them on better terms this time out jockey Mason Paetel takes off a valuable looking 5lb which only enhances his good looking claims here must be considered in a race of this nature

Grand Duchess Olga lines up off a mark of 60 and looks poised to go close after a solid run of staying efforts on the all-weather. She was narrowly denied over this course and distance in January, shaping like the best horse in the race before being collared late, and now gets the same conditions again. With stamina in abundance and track form to match, she sets a clear standard in a modest apprentice handicap. If given a well-judged ride, she should be bang there at the finish.
4th last time out was an improved effort for the yard. Becoming well handicapped and looks well drawn. Most of the others are out of sorts
Winner over course and distance in January. Mostly solid efforts in defeat since including when only beaten a length in 5th last time and very unlikely to be far away once again.

Phoenix Beach is on the hunt for a second win this month and looks dangerous dropped back into Class 6 company off a mark of 62. He scorched home over course and distance on March 11 and ran with credit in stronger company last time despite being drawn wide. Back in calmer waters and with ideal conditions, he has the speed and form to blow this apart.

Bajan Blue steps into handicaps off a mark of 68 and looks very well treated based on the promise of her return at Southwell. She cruised into contention that day before the lack of a recent run told, and now steps up in trip with fitness on her side. This is a weaker race, and she’s got the profile of a filly who could leave this grade behind quickly. If she’s anywhere near as good as she looked on debut, they won’t see which way she went.
Won three starts ago. The small field will suit and has an obvious chance for me. Does need to bounce back, however, but the trip suits.

Supreme Sovereign, a three-year-old gelding trained by Charles Hills, made an impressive debut at Southwell in November 2024, defeating an experienced rival over seven furlongs. He now steps up to 1 mile 142 yards in the 6:00 PM race at Wolverhampton, carrying a penalty for his previous win. With Jason Watson retaining the ride, he looks well-positioned to maintain his unbeaten record. ￼
Been off the track for months but ran in a good maiden at Newmarket on debut, so had to be useful to be running there. Switch to AW can help and looks well-bred.

This 3 year old Maiden with 2 runs under her belt, finished 9th out of 11 at Southwell, where she was a 40/1 long shot. After a break of 138 days, she is expected to return rejuvenated, and with jockey Kieran O'Neill, who is experienced on this track, she has a good chance. A bet each-way at 100/1 could yield a nice return.

Magna Grecia Star ran well on debut running smoothly through the race, then just ran out of ideas late. Now she knows her job, steps into a soft maiden, and gets Rossa Ryan to do the steering. James Tate doesn’t waste runs at Wolverhampton, and this looks like a straightforward assignment. Expect her to cruise into it and finish the job this time.
Not sure about the trainer's SR with first-time-out horses, but this one looks well-bred and doesn't look the hardest race to be winning. The draw should help.

Beta Reader looked like a filly on the up when grinding out victory over this course and distance last week, and she’s turned out quickly under a 6-pound penalty before the handicapper can catch up. She’s uncomplicated, stays well, and clearly handles the surface, which is more than can be said for most of these. With Johnston’s yard firing and confidence high, she’s got every chance of backing it up in a race lacking much form.

Party Bear is the obvious choice after her fine 2nd at this course over 6 months ago, only beaten a head. She has now been freshened up again as that run was 70 days ago and is stepped up in trip, which will suit.

Kathleen’s Glory steps into handicaps off 66 and looks like a classic Gosden project??'three quiet runs, now ready to show her hand. She’s bred to be better than this grade and gets a very winnable opening mark for her first go in a nursery field. With cheekpieces on for the first time and the yard in strong form, this could be the night she makes her move.

An interesting looking class 5 handicap on a Saturday evening with my vote going to Maids Head a very consistent daughter of Pinatubo who was last seen at Kempton 17 days ago where finishing a very respectable 3rd/8 and is most certainly entitled to strip fitter this time out as that was her return run after a 107 day break and should also be a lot sharper at the finish this time out currently operating on an unchanged mark of 68 Maids Head looks poised to strike here and also has a handy draw coming out of gate 2 here at Wolverhampton which should put her in the perfect challenging position and as i metion above she is likely to be a lot sharper at the finish here today jockey Benoit D L Sayette takes the ride and can give Marco Botti's inmate a promising ride here at Wolverhampton very much one to consider . Respected .
Three runs so far and has shown promise. Very unexposed, so can still improve bundles. The draw will help, as will the CD.

Triumphed in a novice race at Brighton last October, but since then, he has only delivered one decent performance on all-weather tracks. His most recent outing for a new trainer was disappointing, as he finished last of 10 in a handicap at Southwell 35 days ago. Nevertheless, the 3-year-old could pull off an upset with Kieran O'Neil aboard, who has notched up 54 victories at Wolverhampton in the last 5 years. With odds of 33/1, I'm particularly interested in his potential for a placing, and given O'Neil's tally of 169 places at Wolverhampton, I think it's worth placing an each-way bet.

I can't resist a small each way bet on this well-drawn horse, which has shown nothing in his last two runs. But prior to that, he was a half-length second on his only previous run over course and distance. The horse led until late on and races off the same mark here. Clearly, a reproduction of that form would make a mockery of the 50/1 quote here. He even has the favorable low draw again, so hopefully, he'll set the pace again and attempt to fend off the late challengers.

Sceptic finally clicked last time, storming clear over this trip here just 11 days ago, and now turns up under a 5-pound penalty that still leaves him below last year’s peak. He travelled like a different horse that day and looked full of running past the line, suggesting there’s more to come now he’s found his rhythm. In a race full of out-of-form types, he arrives with momentum and confidence and looks set for a big run.

234 form figures recently, so it does need to improve again to win. But it was winning races before that, and this CD is likely to suit. The main market dangers haven't been in the best of form recently.

This 3-year-old colt made a winning racecourse debut for trainer R. Varian over one mile at this course 15 days ago. He ran on well in the closing stages despite showing signs of greenness to beat the well-backed K. R. Burke-trained Nordic Norm by 2 1/4 lengths. With improvement likely and J. Mitchell back in the saddle, he can follow up today.
Something amiss last time out, went backwards from debut 3rd. If recapturing that form, should be bang there today. Billy is on board.

Too Much is interesting at the top of the weights here. Last time out he tackled a stronger to 75 contest and didn’t disgrace himself at all, finishing just over three lengths behind the winner despite having traffic issues in the straight. That was off 66 and he runs off 65 here, plus he’s got a capable 5lb claimer on board, so he’s effectively 6lb better off for that effort. His sole win came over 7f but he’s shaped like a mile will suit, especially if he’s allowed to sit handier. This drop in class feels significant. He’s been running with credit in better company and now faces a field where a repeat of that last run could see him right in the mix. If the pace is fair and he gets a smoother passage, he should go close.

Billy rides this one and looks to be riding out of his skin before the season starts. The horse looks like one of the ones to beat and with the least concerns out of my three contenders (including Broken Spear, Pallas Lord). They both have trainer concerns and aren't the correct price. This is overpriced and should run a cracking race.

Winner over a mile here in January. Somewhat inconsistent since, but ran okay when not beaten far in 5th last time and is of interest this evening on this rare drop to 7 furlongs, as won over course and distance off 7lb higher just over a year ago.

Trais Fluors is a real veteran and not without a touch of class, especially in a race like this. He’s a nine-time winner, including in Listed company back in the day, and while those days are behind him, he’s still more than capable at this sort of level. His recent efforts suggest there’s still some spark when he stayed on steadily over 7f here last time in a race that wasn’t really run to suit, and stepping back up to a mile looks the right move. He’s now 2lb lower than when fourth in a stronger to 75 back in January, and this to 65 is a fair bit weaker on paper. He’s well drawn to sit handy if they want, and the booking of a jockey who knows him well is no bad thing. He’ll need things to fall right, but for me he’s got the back class to make him interesting at a nice price. Not one to rule out lightly.
Has many wins, but all over 6f for this stable. But has won at the trip before for a different yard and has the speed to win this. Well drawn.

Inns Of Fear is stepping onto the Newcastle track with a fair bit of buzz. This colt showed promise over in Ireland, snagging a second place at Dundalk over a mile. Now under the guidance of George Boughey and sporting a first-time tongue strap, he's dropping back to 6 furlongs, which could be right up his alley. With Billy Loughnane taking the reins, there's a sense that Inns Of Fear is primed for a strong performance.

Miakoda's been knocking on the door for a while now, hasn't he? This 3yo gelding has been in the mix, placing in three of his eleven starts. While he hasn't quite found that winning formula yet, his consistent performances suggest he's got the potential to break his maiden soon.

Triple Wishes makes her handicap debut off a mark of 55 following three quiet runs in maiden company, though her latest fourth at Newcastle offered a glimmer of promise. Beaten three lengths in a small field over six furlongs, she shaped as though a stronger pace and extra distance could unlock more. Her pedigree, by Expert Eye out of Three Coins, points toward improvement at seven furlongs. The first-time hood could help her settle, and in a weak race with no standout form, she has the profile of one who might progress now switched to handicaps.

Gelded son of Magna Grecia who was last seen at this venue over the mile trip 12 days ago where finishing 8th/9 however I'm willing to excuse that run as he looked to be in need of it as he was returning from a 80 day break on the occasion currently operating on a falling mark of 50 Nigel Tinkler's inmate is well off the handicappers radar and it is very well possible he is better than a mark of 50 heading down the handicap route in very good time as he is off the handicappers radar for the time being it would be a wise and profitable move to catch him running well at this stage as he is a valuable looking E/W price at the time of writing jockey Billy Loughnane takes the ride that being a positive booking . Respected .
5th on handicap debut, probably in a similar race here. Needs to improve, but hood is fitted and trainer does well here.

Lord Abama, a six-year-old gelding trained by Michael Dods, has shown consistent form over six furlongs at Newcastle. His latest win came on November 5, 2024, in a Class 6 handicap over this course and distance off a mark of 62. He is now rated 65, just 3 pounds higher, indicating he remains competitively handicapped. Notably, he has secured three wins and eight placings from 28 starts, reflecting a respectable 11% win rate. His familiarity with the track and proven ability at the distance suggest he could be a strong contender in the upcoming Class 5 event.
Goes well fresh. Has put in big efforts in the past. Recent form was poor, but given a break and could surprise at big odds here.

Sir Garfield returns to seven furlongs at Newcastle, a trip that has previously brought out the best in him, including a decisive win at Ayr off a mark of 63. He is now rated 65, just 2 pounds higher, and that leaves him fairly treated on past evidence. His recent effort over six furlongs at this track was too poor to be true, dropping out tamely after showing early pace, but he may have needed the run after a 146-day break. He is better judged on his consistent turf campaign last year, where he travelled strongly in several competitive Class 6 handicaps and responded well under pressure. If stripping fitter now, and with the return to a more suitable trip, he has claims in a race where few arrive in strong form.

Urban Dandy comes here in red-hot form, having bolted up over a mile at Newcastle just 12 days ago off a mark of 48. That win came on the back of a narrow second at the same venue, and he now bids for a quick double under just a 5-pound penalty. Dropping to seven furlongs poses no issue given how strongly he travelled last time, and he remains well treated against this level of opposition. With confidence high and conditions ideal, he looks the one to beat.
Won two starts back. Has won over this distance in the past also, so it's no problem. Probably just needs slight improvement to be seen winning again here. Well drawn.

Dandy Lichious is threatening to strike after two eye-catching thirds over seven furlongs, including a strong finish here at Newcastle in January where he was closing late from off the pace. He’s now just 1 pound above his last winning mark, which came over this trip at Dundalk, and looks primed to deliver with conditions to suit. With the race likely to set up for a closer, he shapes as a big player in a modest Class 6.

Dark Kestrel is thriving at present and looks a major player dropping back into Class 5 company. He ran a cracker here nine days ago in a Class 4, flashing home for second behind a progressive type and confirming he’s still on the up off a mark of 74. That followed a solid run in a strong field and a course win in the autumn, making him one of the most consistent five-furlong operators on the all-weather this winter. Back at his optimum trip and track, he sets the standard and rates a live contender.
2-2 at the track, but it's at 6f. Anyway, must have plenty of speed and can easily take this if back to that form.

South Shore's form on paper does look off putting however looks can be deceiving and a deeper analysis of this individual tells a whole different story was last seen at this venue racing at the 6 furlong trip where finishing last of 8 however he was returning from a 152 day break and most certainly needed that run likely to be more adjusted back home as he joined this yard last year from the Karl Burke stable and he did win of a mark of 75 with that stable he is now operating on mark 68 now surely a 4yo gelded son of Blue Point who was capable of winning of a mark of 75 last year is likely to have a very big performance in the locker of a mark of 68 and he did switch yards at a crucial stage of his career a monster E/W price at the time of writing he is worth the interest and if on song as he should be he could cause a shock in the finale and if he is to settle for a silver medal at the very least it wouldn't be so bad given the odds on offer
Has to give piles of weight away because he's rated 148, but he can take this if jumping better. 5 wins from 17 over fences, and that's better than some. Small field to suit.
